subject: Recap: cost & TCO — batching/caching levers and proposed commit path
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia@cleargate.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: cost & TCO — batching/caching levers and proposed commit path

Alicia — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have the alignment and clear next steps. I kept this focused on the economics and gating approach we discussed.

Key pain points you shared
- Monthly inference spend is trending ~2.1M tokens/month for your core customer flow; spikes up to ~3.8M during peak promotions.
- Current budget for a pilot proof-of-value is ~USD 12k–15k/month; procurement prefers a short, low-commitment trial before any larger contract.
- Latency target: 90th perc latency < 450ms for completion-sensitive endpoints.

Goals we agreed
- Validate end-to-end quality at 95% acceptance on a 3k prompt testset.
- Demonstrate 30–45% unit cost improvement vs current baseline through batching + prefix KV caching.
- Provide a concrete commit path (pilot → reserved capacity) with clear ROI and rollout gates.

Economic highlights & levers (high level)
- Batching: expected token-cost reduction 18–28% for your traffic shape when we enable continuous batching with a 100–300ms wait window combined with request coalescing.
- Prefix/KV caching: for your repeat-prompt patterns (~42% reuse), caching should cut decoder token spend by ~22% observed in similar customers.
- Model selection: recommending 2 model variants for pilot — a throughput-optimized quantized variant (lowest unit-cost) and a quality-controlled float variant to validate edge cases.

Pilot proposal (recommended)
1) 3-week technical validation (no-charge for infra variance): integration, sample test-suite, and live A/B for 2 endpoints.
2) 6-week paid pilot (budget anchor: $12k/month) with the following deliverables:
   - Weekly token-econ snapshots and a mid-pilot check (savings vs baseline).
   - One canary rollout rule (traffic % flip) to validate model variant for production.
   - Final TCO brief that outlines expected monthly unit costs at scale and suggested reserved capacity commit (3–12 months).

Concrete asks from ClearGate to size the pilot accurately
- Rough monthly token volume by endpoint (if you can share a 14-day sample or aggregate by endpoint).
- Peak QPS and expected concurrency during promotions.
- Any compliance artifacts that would affect private deployment (we can run hosted for the pilot if easier).

Attachments: I attached a short token-econ worksheet that shows the baseline assumptions and two scenario estimates (optimistic / conservative).

Next steps I propose
- Alicia: confirm whether the $12k/month pilot budget is viable and send the sample 14-day traffic extract (S3 link or CSV).
- Marissa: I’m looping you to draft a concise SOW (pilot-sow-draft.pdf) and cost-scenarios.csv for the pricing options.
- Karthik: please prepare a short ops checklist for canary rollout and model variant configs.

If that matches your read, I’ll queue up the SOW and a DocuSign placeholder so procurement can review quickly.

Thanks again — short exec summary and the worksheet attached.

—
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: cleargate-token-econ-worksheet.xlsx
From: Alicia Ramos <alicia@cleargate.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: cost & TCO — batching/caching levers and proposed commit path

Thanks Markus — this is helpful and aligned with our internal notes. A few clarifications:
- We can commit up to $12k/month for a short pilot; stretching to $15k would need an exec sign-off.
- I can share a 14-day anonymized token/export for the two endpoints by end of day Wednesday (will send S3 link).
- For the pilot, procurement wants a one-page SOW + a clear cancel clause (we’ll need to see minimum notice).

High level ask from my side: can you show a conservative scenario where savings net to >= 20% within the paid pilot (so our stakeholders see a plausible ROI quickly)? If your scenario shows it’s only achievable after reserved commit, please indicate what that commit looks like ($ / month / term).

Appreciate the quick turn — Alicia

Subject: Re: Recap: cost & TCO — batching/caching levers and proposed commit path

Markus / Alicia — looping in a concise SOW approach and a conservative cost scenario. Quick notes from our side:
- Conservative scenario (attached cost-scenarios.csv) assumes 12% batching uplift and 18% caching effective reduction; optimistic scenario assumes up to 25%+ from combined levers. We chart both in the CSV.
- SOW skeleton: 3-week integration + 6-week paid pilot, deliverables as listed in Markus’ note. Cancellation: 14-day notice post-paid pilot, pilot pricing pro-rated.
- Proposed pilot commercial: $12,000/month for 6 weeks (billed as one invoice). If ClearGate opts-in to a 3-month reserved commit after pilot, we layout 10–15% discount tiers depending on term and baseline commit.

Action for ops: Karthik, please draft the canary rollout checklist (model variant mapping + rollback criteria) and a short runbook snippet.

Alicia — I’ll attach the SOW PDF and the cost scenarios in this thread. If you want, we can add a table showing expected break-even month at three commit levels ($12k, $25k, $50k).

—
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: pilot-sow-draft.pdf, cost-scenarios.csv
